title: Character concept
appliesWhen: The product shows characters: game characters, a mascot, an assistant's avatar, or illustrated guides. Left out when no character is shown.

questions.ask: Which characters are needed, and which are main characters (seen most, or central to the product)?
questions.why: Main characters get the full design; the others follow their pattern.

questions.ask: For each main character: what role do they play, and what should a person feel on seeing them?
questions.why: Each concept is judged against its role and feeling; without them every variation is equally right.

questions.ask: Which art style (for example realistic, stylised, flat illustration, pixel art), and which existing characters or works feel right or wrong?
questions.why: References show what words cannot; the wrong ones rule directions out early.

questions.ask: Will the characters be drawn in 2D or built as 3D models, and which moves and expressions do they need (for example idle, walk, talk, happy, sad)?
questions.why: 3D characters continue in the 3D assets pipeline; every move and expression is art to make and a state the product switches between.

questions.ask: What is the smallest size each character is shown at, in pixels on the smallest named screen (for example an icon, a map marker, a chat avatar)?
questions.why: A character that cannot be told apart at its smallest size fails where it is seen most.

questions.ask: Is there an existing character, mascot or licensed property the concepts must follow?
questions.why: An existing character is an input to follow; a licence is an owner decision.

questions.ask: Who is the audience, and are there content limits or ways people must or must not be shown?
questions.why: Characters represent people; the owner sets these limits, not the designer.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each main character was chosen from at least two rendered variations, and the choice is recorded.

check.how: At least two variations of each main character are image files in the product repository, and the character record names the one chosen.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each main character has a turnaround: front, side and back views at the same scale, as image files.

check.how: Each main character's sheet is opened; the three views are present, drawn at the same height, and show the same design.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each main character can be told apart from the other main characters by silhouette alone.

check.how: The main characters are shown side by side as solid single-colour shapes with no labels; a reviewer who has read the character sheets names each one correctly.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each character can still be told apart at the smallest size named in the Q&A.

check.how: Each character is rendered at that pixel size beside the others at the same size; a reviewer names each one correctly.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each character sheet has a flat-colour front view (no shading) and lists the character's base colours as colour values, and every colour area of that view uses one of them.

check.how: A colour picker samples one point in each colour area of the flat-colour front view image; a sampled value not on the sheet's list is listed.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every move and expression the Q&A named for a character is listed on its sheet and drawn at least once as a key pose.

check.how: The moves and expressions in the Q&A answer are compared with the sheet's list and its drawn poses; a named move or expression with no pose is listed.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Where the project picked the storyline pipeline, every character on its cast list has a concept that fits the one-line role given there.

check.how: The storyline's cast list is compared with the character sheets; a character with no sheet, or a sheet that contradicts the role, is listed. Passes without a comparison when the storyline pipeline is not picked.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Where the Q&A named an existing character or property, the concept follows it and differs only where the owner agreed.

check.how: Each concept is set beside the named reference; every difference is listed, and one without the owner's recorded agreement fails. Passes without a comparison when the Q&A named nothing to follow.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each character is recorded as original, with the references used to make it, or as licensed, with its licence.

check.how: The character record has one line per character saying original or licensed, with the references or the licence; a character with no line fails.

criteria.mustBeTrue: No character goes beyond the content limits or the ways of showing people the Q&A set.

check.how: Each character sheet is read against the Q&A answer on audience and limits; a character that goes beyond them is listed.

outputs.title: Character variations
outputs.what: At least two rendered variations of each main character, for the owner to choose from.

outputs.title: Character sheets
outputs.what: One sheet per main character: the turnaround, a flat-colour front view, the key poses for each move and expression, the colour values, the silhouette and the smallest-size view, and whether it is 2D or 3D.

outputs.title: Character record
outputs.what: Each character with its role, the variation chosen and when, and whether it is original (with references) or licensed (with the licence).

logic: Each move and expression on a sheet is a state the product switches between, with a test that each one plays.
Characters a user can choose or change are settings the product stores for each user.
assets: 2D characters: sprite sheets or vector files for each move and expression, at each size shown.
3D characters continue in the 3D assets pipeline as models built from the turnaround.
runtime: Sprite sheet size grows with frames per move times moves times sizes: the move list sets the image memory and download size.
Each animated character on screen costs memory and frame time; the most characters on screen at once, set in system design, sets that budget.
